weaknesses: The rationale is stronger than a purely free-slot argument, but it underweights the cumulative load of the visible week: daily morning training, several afternoon training sessions, two final exams, and study blocks. The added Wednesday social event at 2027-06-16 19:30-20:30 follows Morning Recovery & Mobility, Business Law study, and Afternoon Tactical Session on the same day.

The Friday dinner at 2027-06-18 19:30-22:00 follows Morning Light Activation at 07:30-09:00, the Business Law Final Exam at 10:00-12:00, lunch at 12:30-13:30, and Afternoon Technical Training at 16:30-18:30. The one-hour gap before dinner may be enough in some contexts, but the plan does not substantiate travel, showering, changing, decompression, or arrival logistics after training.

The proposal acknowledges that Friday venue-to-home travel is unknown and that the 23:00 sleep target cannot be fully verified, but it still treats the full dinner as the preferred option without explaining why the risk to recovery after a dense exam/training day is acceptable.

The alternative 'attend only the Friday dinner' is identified as simpler but is not clearly weighed against the actual human-quality concern introduced by the selected plan: adding a Wednesday commitment during exam week plus a full Friday evening commitment after a high-load day.

critic_evaluation.feedback: The proposal is generally coherent and preserves protected events, and the Wednesday addition is reasonably limited. The main practical risk is not a calendar conflict but cumulative manageability: the user has a demanding visible week with repeated training, study, and two exams, then the plan adds two social commitments. Friday is the most concerning because the dinner starts only one hour after a 16:30-18:30 training session and ends at 22:00, while the rationale itself says the post-dinner travel and 23:00 sleep target are not fully verified. The Proposer should reconsider or substantiate whether the Friday evening plan realistically allows post-training cleanup, travel, dinner attendance, return home, and recovery without undermining the protected rest pattern. With fuller context, the same operations might still be acceptable, but the current rationale does not fully support the human feasibility of the Friday evening sequence.

plausibility_review.suggested_improvement: Reconsider the Friday dinner in light of post-training logistics and recovery, or provide grounded context showing that travel, hygiene, decompression, and return before the intended sleep routine are realistically accommodated. Also briefly justify why adding the Wednesday social hour remains worthwhile given the cumulative exam-week load.
